fact: Namclear has joined the SADC TCIB network operated with PayInc, connecting Namibian banks and authorised non-bank institutions to near-instant cross-border push payments.
Namclear says TCIB services will allow consumers and businesses to send money between Namibia, South Africa and other Common Monetary Area countries.

The Bank of Namibia's Directive PSDIR-10 says cross-border low-value electronic transfers within the Common Monetary Area are currently settled through a temporary SADC-RTGS arrangement, to cease by 31 March 2027 in favour of TCIB.

The Bank of Namibia's Directive PSDIR-10 requires payment service providers to execute low-value Common Monetary Area transfers through the regional TCIB scheme from 1 April 2027, after the SADC-RTGS stopgap ends on 31 March 2027.

The CMA Cross-border Payments Oversight Committee's paper of 31 July 2024 says rand cross-border low-value EFTs within the Common Monetary Area, including Namibia, run through an interim supplementary-file solution in place since 1 October 2019 and still in use.

The CMA committee's paper of 31 July 2024 says banks route low-value cross-border EFTs within the CMA, Namibia among its four members, through the SADC real-time gross settlement system under the interim arrangement, to move to a designated retail system such as TCIB from 1 April 2027.

The South African Reserve Bank said that from 30 September 2024 low-value electronic funds transfers, debit and credit payments among Eswatini, Lesotho, Namibia and South Africa are treated as cross-border transactions with greater due diligence.

The South African Reserve Bank directive says low-value cross-border electronic funds transfers within the Common Monetary Area (Eswatini, Lesotho, Namibia, South Africa) are currently executed through SADC-RTGS.

The South African Reserve Bank directive says Common Monetary Area low-value transfers, including this country's, run through the SADC-RTGS regional system and must move to the TCIB scheme by April 2027.
